title: The bent woman (Luke 13:10–17)
hookLine: eighteen years bent over, healed on the sabbath, and she stands straight

lines: LOOK AT THE FLOOR. STAY THERE.
EIGHTEEN YEARS OF FEET AND DUST.
cards: Try this for a moment. Let your head drop and your back curl until you're looking at the floor. Stay there.
You can see feet, and dust, and the hems of other people's clothes. You can't see a face unless someone bends down to you.

Now imagine that for eighteen years: going to the market like that, going to the synagogue like that. Luke says there was a woman who lived this way, and one sabbath Jesus was teaching in her synagogue.

teach.b: Luke describes her carefully: "there was a woman, who had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years: and she was bent down, neither could she look upwards at all." She doesn't ask for anything. Luke only says she was there.
Jesus sees her and calls her over: "Woman, thou art delivered from thy infirmity." He lays his hands on her, and immediately she's made straight, and she glorifies God. Then a complication.
The ruler of the synagogue is indignant, because it's the sabbath. There are six days for work, he tells the crowd. Come and be healed on those.
It's fair to see what he's protecting. Keeping the sabbath holy was, and is, a deep act of faithfulness for Jews. Jesus answers from inside that same faithfulness.
Every one of you unties his ox or his donkey on the sabbath and leads it to water.

teach.h: THE OX UNTIED ON THE SABBATH.
teach.b: And this woman, a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has bound these eighteen years, shouldn't she be untied on the sabbath day?
Daughter of Abraham: the title gives her back her full place among God's people.
In Jesus' reading, the sabbath is exactly the day for setting someone free. Luke ends with the crowd rejoicing at all the glorious things he was doing.

how: Catholics pray for the sick at Mass and through the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick, in which the priest lays hands on the sick person, as Jesus did here.

o: a long weakness or illness of the body
a hospital ward where the sick are kept
a lack of faith that keeps you from prayer

games.q: you lead the synagogue. a teacher has just healed a woman on the sabbath, and the crowd is buzzing. what do you say?
o: there are six days for healing. come on those.
praise God, and invite him to teach again.
games.why: he says come on the other six days. Jesus answers: you untie your ox on the sabbath, so why not a daughter of Abraham?

practice: If you're able, stand; if not, sit tall, and start bent, head dropped and shoulders curled, breathing there a moment.
Then slowly unroll your spine until your head rises and you're looking straight ahead, and think of one thing you're grateful for today.
If you pray, give thanks to God the way she did; if you don't, simply let yourself feel glad to be upright.

wordCard.voice: Infirmity. Eighteen years unable to look up, healed by Jesus on the sabbath and called a daughter of Abraham. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: she stood up. Eighteen years of looking at the floor, and then she looked up. That's day four hundred sixty-six.
